subject: Initial org & API access for Acme Energy - next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan@acme-energy.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial org & API access for Acme Energy - next steps

Jordan —

Great to meet you yesterday. Next step from our side is to create your tenant and wire up the access patterns you mentioned so your team can start hitting the API and onboarding models. I sketched a short list below so we can align on scope and timing: 

- Create tenant: acme-energy-prod (default region: us-west)
- Create initial project: acme-energy/core-integration
- Provision service account for CI (token-based service key)
- Create scoped API key for client-side demos (short TTL, restrictive quotas)
- Invite admin users and SSO (SAML) configuration if you want IdP-managed roles
- Confirm retention/audit log settings and data residency for the pilot

Attached is a one-page onboarding checklist and the service-account instruction PDF we typically use. Proposed timeline: provisioning + invites today, SSO metadata exchange by Friday, verification testing early next week.

Questions for you now: who should be the tenant admin (name + email), and do you prefer SSO (SAML) or Redwoods-managed accounts for the initial pilot? Also confirm if you want a dedicated billing contact or if we should bill the main account.

Once I have that, I’ll hand off the provisioning to Monica on our CS team to complete the setup and send the invites.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: ACME_onboarding_checklist.xlsx, ACME_service-account-instructions.pdf
From: Jordan Myers <jordan@acme-energy.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial org & API access for Acme Energy - next steps

Thanks Sean —

Quick answers: we prefer SSO (SAML) for admin accounts. Tenant admin will be me (Jordan Myers <jordan@acme-energy.com>). Our infra lead (ops@acme-energy.com) should also be an admin.

A couple of implementation questions before you hand off:
- For the service account used by our CI pipeline, can Redwood provide a rotating token or do we need to implement rotation on our side?
- Can you scope API keys so they can only call generation endpoints and not billing APIs?
- We will need TTL guidance for demo keys (what's reasonable for client demos).

If you need our IdP metadata I can ask ops to send the SAML metadata, but prefer to exchange it after you create the tenant so callback URLs are correct.

Jordan
Jordan Myers
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Energy
jordan@acme-energy.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial org & API access for Acme Energy - provisioning plan (hand-off)

Sean / Laura —

I’ll take the provisioning tasks once Jordan confirms admin names (he did). Plan below — I’ll execute and post the tenant details in this thread when done.

Provisioning checklist (what I will do):
1) Create tenant: acme-energy-prod (region: us-west-2) and register org id ACME-123 in our console.
2) Create project: acme-energy/core-integration with default model routing to redwood-curated/gptx-small for pilot traffic.
3) Create service account: acme-ci-service (role: service-admin). I will generate a service token with 90d TTL and enable rotation policy: auto-rotate every 60 days; we will issue instructions to ops to fetch rotated tokens via our admin UI or vault.
4) Create demo API key: acme-demo-key-01 with restricted scopes (generation only), daily request quota 50k tokens, TTL 24 hours for first week.
5) Invite users: Jordan Myers (Admin), ops@acme-energy.com (Admin), and an initial developer (dev@acme-energy.com) as Developer role.
6) SSO: I will create the SAML app placeholder and send ACS/Entity ID back to Jordan to exchange IdP metadata.
7) Audit & retention: set audit logs to 180 days (per our pilot default) and enable token-level cost attribution for the project.

Notes / decisions needed from Sean before I start:
- Confirm billing contact (we will default to Jordan if you want to keep that)
- Confirm whether to enable KV cache for pilot (saves cost but may require client-side consent for caching prompts)

I’ll run these changes in the staging account first and post the tenant admin link once ready.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Jordan —

Thanks for confirming — Monica will run the setup. Below are concrete steps you/ops should follow once you receive the tenant invite and SAML placeholders. I’m pasting Monica’s plan inline for visibility:

On Thu, 5 Mar 2026 at 11:30 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> I’ll take the provisioning tasks once Jordan confirms admin names (he did). Plan below — I’ll execute and post the tenant details in this thread when done.

> 1) Create tenant: acme-energy-prod...
> 2) Create project: acme-energy/core-integration...
> 3) Create service account: acme-ci-service (role: service-admin)...
> 4) Create demo API key: acme-demo-key-01...
> 5) Invite users: Jordan Myers (Admin), ops@acme-energy.com (Admin), dev@acme-energy.com (Developer)
> 6) SSO: I will create the SAML app placeholder and send ACS/Entity ID back to Jordan to exchange IdP metadata.
> 7) Audit & retention: set audit logs to 180 days...

Action items for Acme ops when you receive the SAML placeholder:
- Export IdP metadata (XML) and return to me (or upload to: https://console.redwood.ai/setup/tenants/ACME-123)
- Confirm the list of initial developers who should get Developer role (reply with emails)
- For CI tokens: either accept the auto-rotate policy (recommended) or tell us how you want rotation handled (we support AWS Secrets Manager or manual download).

Security notes: demo keys are scoped to generation-only and cannot access billing or org-level settings. Service tokens are scoped at the project level and we will limit network egress in our firewall rules.

I’ll check back after Monica posts the tenant URL. If anything is urgent, reply-all or call my line.

Thanks,
Sean
